content: Supervised and unsupervised learning are the most common approaches to learning from data. With supervised learning, a model learns from labeled data (e.g., social media messages labeled by sentiment) to infer (or predict) these labels from unlabeled texts. In contrast, unsupervised learning uses unlabeled data. Supervised approaches are especially suitable when we have a clear definition of the concept of interest and when labels are available (either annotated or native to the data). Unsupervised approaches, such as topic models, are especially useful for exploration. In this setting, conceptualization and operationalization may occur simultaneously, with theory emerging from the data BIBREF26 . Unsupervised approaches are also used when there is a clear way of measuring a concept, often based on strong assumptions. For example, BIBREF3 measure “surprise” in an analysis of Darwin's reading decisions based on the divergence between two probability distributions.
